claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to gather some information about you and your children.

Let me start with a basic question:

**How many children are you inquiring about, and what are their names?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'm wondering if I can claim Child Benefit. I have one child - my son Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! I'm assessing eligibility for your son, Alex.

To help me determine if you're eligible, I need to understand your circumstances a bit better.

**What is Alex's date of birth?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex is 17 years old - he was born in January 2008.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. That helps me understand Alex's age.

**Does Alex live with you, or does he live with someone else?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good, thank you for confirming that.

**Are you currently a UK resident, and do you have the right to reside in the UK?** (This relates to your eligibility as the claimant, rather than Alex's circumstances.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - I'm in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that confirmation.

Before I make my final assessment, let me check the specific eligibility rules to ensure I give you accurate information.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the eligibility rules I've just reviewed, I need to ask one more important question about Alex:

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training (such as school, college, university, or a training scheme)?**

This is important because while you normally need to have a child under 16 to qualify for Child Benefit, there's an exception for 16-17 year-olds who remain in approved education or training.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he's still in sixth form studying for his A-levels.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you for that information. I now have all the details I need to make a determination.

Based on the information you've provided:

- Alex is 17 years old and was born in January 2008
- He lives with you at home
- He is currently in approved education (sixth form, studying for A-levels)
- You are a UK resident in Manchester

According to the Child Benefit eligibility rules, you normally qualify if you're responsible for a child under 16 and you live in the UK. However, there's an important exception: **you'll normally still qualify for Child Benefit if your child is under 20 and they stay in approved education or training.**

Since Alex is 17 and remains in approved education (sixth form), you meet the eligibility criteria for Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Good news! You are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.**

You can claim Child Benefit because:
- You live in the UK and are responsible for Alex
- Alex is 17 years old and living with you
- He is in approved education (sixth form)
- The rules allow Child Benefit for children aged 16-19 who remain in full-time approved education or training

This eligibility will continue as long as Alex remains in approved education and is under 20 years old. If he leaves education before then, you would be able to continue receiving Child Benefit for 20 weeks if he registers with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services.

If you'd like to make a claim, you can do so through the official Child Benefit application process. Is there anything else you'd like to know?
